name: GRAND
full_name: Giant Radio Array for Neutrino Detection
summary: GRAND includes GP300 near Dunhuang, China, prototypes at Auger in Argentina and Nançay in France, and future worldwide arrays. This multimessenger radio project's Chinese and overseas prototypes must not be conflated with a completed global facility.
detection_principle: Ground radio antennas measure extensive air showers, focusing on upward-going / near-horizontal tau-decay showers from Earth-skimming tau neutrinos, while also measuring ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays and gamma rays.

sites.name: GRANDProto300
sites.location: Gobi Desert near Dunhuang, Gansu; prototype deployment

sites.name: Complete GRAND multi-array system
sites.location: Multiple candidate sites worldwide, not yet finalized

results.summary: Prototype operation and cosmic-ray-candidate studies are public; no superheavy-dark-matter search result from the complete GRAND array.
Theoretical work forecasts the potential of radio neutrino arrays such as GRAND to constrain heavy dark-matter decay.

science_scope: Searches cosmic gamma-ray, antiparticle or neutrino spectra, directions and fluxes for indirect signatures of dark-matter annihilation, decay or related new physics. Conventional astrophysical sources and propagation can produce similar signals, requiring background modeling; design sensitivity is not a measured limit or discovery.

media.caption: Detection-principle diagram for GRAND10k from Figure 16 of the original GRAND design paper: a mountainside antenna array receives radio signals from cosmic-ray or Earth-skimming tau-neutrino-induced air showers. Lower-left inset: HorizonAntenna concept. A proposed array design, not a photograph of a completed full array.
